findings.body: When rewritten history causes a fresh conversation, this write retains the previous conversation's `head`: `_record` merges fields into the existing record (`src/forge/codex.py:386–390`). If the replacement turn crashes, `recover()` logs its recovered status without replacing that stale `head`. The subsequent ancestry check then rejects the replacement conversation because the old conversation's ending commit is still outside the rewritten history. Thus the next `forge work` discards a resumable conversation even though its own history hasn't changed. Clear the previous conversation's ending commit when recording a new conversation, and cover a history rewrite followed by a crashed replacement turn.
